seoTitle: Transfer a Squarespace Domain to Hostinger (2026)
metaDescription: Move your domain from Squarespace to Hostinger for better hosting performance, lower costs, and more DNS control — full step-by-step guide.
intro: If you bought your domain through Squarespace but want to host elsewhere, moving it to Hostinger gives you more control over DNS and often lower costs. This guide covers unlocking your domain, getting your authorization code, and finishing the transfer without downtime.

steps.heading: Unlock your domain in Squarespace
steps.body: Before a transfer can start, your domain needs to be unlocked in your Squarespace domain settings.

steps.heading: Find your EPP/authorization code
steps.body: Locate the EPP or authorization code in Squarespace's domain settings — Hostinger will need this to verify the transfer.

steps.heading: Start the transfer in Hostinger
steps.body: In your Hostinger account, begin the domain transfer process and enter your domain along with the authorization code.

steps.heading: Update your DNS settings
steps.body: Once the transfer is initiated, update your DNS records in Hostinger so your website and email keep working during the switch.

steps.heading: Verify the transfer and check for downtime
steps.body: Confirm the domain has moved successfully, and monitor your site to catch any propagation delays before they affect visitors.

faq.question: Why transfer a domain from Squarespace to Hostinger?
faq.answer: Common reasons include better hosting performance, lower costs, and more control over DNS settings than Squarespace offers by default.

faq.question: What is an EPP code and why do I need it?
faq.answer: It's an authorization code that proves you own the domain and authorizes the new registrar to accept the transfer.

faq.question: Will my website go down during the transfer?
faq.answer: Not necessarily — updating DNS settings correctly and timing the switch carefully helps avoid downtime, though some propagation delay is normal.

faq.question: How long does a domain transfer usually take?
faq.answer: Domain transfers commonly take a few days to complete, plus additional time for DNS propagation once it's finished.
